A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLBF research. Their main text, equations, figure, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including identification of the checklist removed in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety evaluations, utility benchmarks, category-level results, and backtracking ablations in Sections 3 and 5 and Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds critic validation, adaptive-attack results, weaker-critic training experiments, and backtracking-efficiency comparisons.

M1.justification: The BSAFE+ data construction, category and backtrack tokens, autoregressive output handling, reward rules, and GRPO objective with SFT guidance remain unchanged. The weaker critic is an experimental configuration of the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds a manually constructed critic-validation set covering different violation locations and severities, and an adaptive GCG scenario targeting backtracking-token suppression. The existing LMSYS, adversarial-attack, and utility benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Circuit Breakers to both LMSYS-MF and LMSYS comparisons across five model configurations; v1 evaluated it in Table 2 only. Section 5.6 adds BSAFE's repeat-and-edit format to a controlled safety and efficiency comparison. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include 100 critic-validation pairs with 43 high-, 38 medium-, and 19 low-severity cases, three critic prompts, RL training with a weaker LLaMA 3 8B critic, backtracking-suppressing adaptive GCG, and identical-data and correction-replay controls for efficiency. These substantially expand the experimental design. Newly stated training hyperparameters document existing experiments rather than establish changed settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained category analysis and backtracking-disabling ablation, v2 tests critic-prompt sensitivity, dependence on critic quality, resistance to targeted adaptive attacks, and the contributions of data construction and backtracking format. Sections 4.2.1, 5.1, 5.5, and 5.6 substantially expand robustness and diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Section 4.2.1 newly reports three samples per critic-validation pair. Removing v1's checklist also removes its explanation that repeated model training for error bars was computationally infeasible. Neither version supplies uncertainty intervals or significance tests for the main results; the weaker-critic experiment does not establish repeated runs under identical settings.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 entries and Tables 2–5 are unchanged. Added results include Circuit Breakers ASRs of 13%–18% on LMSYS-MF and 17%–21% on LMSYS; critic accuracies of 97.6%, 97.6%, and 98.0%; weaker-critic LMSYS ASRs of 2%–4%; and adaptive-GCG ASRs of 4.7% and 4.3%. Section 5.6 adds BSAFE ASRs of 17%–22% and average token savings of 68.3/72.6, or 74.8/79.1 under correction replay. Associated latency savings are estimates.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, SFT loss, reward specification, RL objective, and combined training objective are unchanged. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs, and the new empirical analyses add none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient backtracking, improved SFT data construction, critic-guided RL, stronger safety, and preserved utility. v2 adds supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets weaker-critic results as evidence that gains arise from policy learning rather than critic accuracy alone, and attributes benefits to data construction independently of backtracking format. It also discusses robustness without attack-specific training exposure and practical implications of estimated latency savings. Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 replaces a general reference to supplementary details with A100 80GB hardware, bf16 precision, AdamW, 100-step warmup and cosine decay, SFT/RL learning rates, SFT guidance weight 0.1, 300k augmented examples, and approximately 800 GPU-hours per model. These substantially improve implementation documentation. Appendix A's prompts are unchanged. Checklist removal eliminates explicit non-release disclosures for code/data without demonstrating a release.

R1.justification: The reference list and Related Work section are unchanged. The experimental discussion adds limited differentiation from existing work: Circuit Breakers is described as producing incoherent text when triggered, and the BSAFE comparison distinguishes benefits of data construction from those of correction format.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained verbatim. v2 adds localized explanations and Sections 5.5–5.6, expands the experimental setup paragraph, and removes the appended NeurIPS checklist. The prompt appendix remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains Circuit Breakers rows and an updated caption. Table 3 moves from beneath the utility discussion to a separate, mostly empty page, with other content reflowing. Figure 1, the remaining table designs, and appendix prompt panels are retained; no new figure is introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens previously limited evidence for central properties: critic reliability, robustness to attacks targeting backtracking, and the efficiency advantage over BSAFE. It also supplies important training details absent from v1's main text and prompt-only appendix. These gains materially improve evidential support and reproducibility. Uncertainty estimates remain absent, latency benefits are estimated, and checklist removal loses availability and statistical disclosures, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantive additions.
